<reason>B won by distinguishing tenant qualification from the additional obligations attached to a payment arrangement. A established serious housing-access harms, but repeatedly assumed that agency contracts and conditions were negligible paperwork. B answered the pressure questions directly and exposed A’s unsupported distinction between permissible timing constraints and impermissible contractual objections. A’s closing treated categorical effects as sufficient proof of illegitimate discrimination rather than answering B’s justification for those distinctions.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B’s response to A’s mandatory acceptance of “standard” program terms was decisive: routine terms remain additional obligations on landlords, and an applicant’s qualifications cannot absorb obligations imposed on somebody else. B also explained why individualized screening cannot resolve an objection to a contractual requirement shared by every participant.</best_rebuttal>
